title: Experiment: production-build artifact read, Cache Components enabled and disabled
summary: Two full builds. With cacheComponents ENABLED the route built as "┌ ○ /" and served "VALUE_AT_BUILD_TIME" on the first request; after an external write of a different value it still served "VALUE_AT_BUILD_TIME", and "VALUE_AT_BUILD_TIME" six seconds later. With cacheComponents DISABLED the result was identical: route "┌ ○ /", and the same build-time value on all three requests. In both configurations a later external write did not change what a fresh request returned.

facts.workspace: two dedicated temporary directories, removal verified
facts.network: loopback only for `next start`; npm install reached the public registry

omissions.reason: Requests were made immediately after the external write and again six seconds later. A revalidation window longer than that would not have been seen, so this shows the value is frozen across ten seconds, not that it is frozen forever.

Only the default static outcome was exercised. Whether an explicitly dynamic route, or a read through a dynamic API, reflects external writes was not tested — and that is precisely what the application needs to know next.
One host was available; this is scoped to Windows and cannot be generalised from here.

notes: ⚠️ BOTH CONFIGURATIONS WERE RUN ON PURPOSE. The claim names the cacheComponents-enabled case, and testing only that case would have left the undecided configuration as a third deferral — which is the outcome #80's condition exists to prevent. Running both is what produced the second finding. ⚠️ Host execution: the tier-1 controller could not run this (network for `npm install`, and no long-lived service form — QST-0022). Two disposable workspaces, removal observed rather than trusted, whole process tree terminated between configurations.
